3. **Mean/Median Imputation**: This involves replacing the missing value with the mean or median of the respective column. This method is simple and effective, but can be sensitive to outliers.
4. **Regression Imputation**: This involves using a regression model to predict the missing value based on other variables. This method is more accurate than mean/median imputation but can be computationally expensive.
5. **K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Imputation**: This involves finding the k-nearest neighbors to the observation with the missing value and using their values to impute the missing value. This method is useful when there are complex relationships between variables.
